mainTopic: Kneading with a שינוי on שבת, and whether a person's nature and fate depend on מזל
overview: The גמרא identifies the lenient view on kneading as רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's, but limits it: kneading or mixing is allowed only with a שינוי (a change from the weekday method). Three times it asks 'how does one change it?' The answers are kneading little by little, putting the שתית in before the vinegar, and stirring animal feed crosswise or pouring it between vessels. A story about לוי teaches that one may knead feed but not stuff it into an animal's mouth, unless the animal cannot eat by itself. Notebooks of זעירי and לוי add rulings about animal feed, and tell how רבי could not stop people kneading שתיתא because they relied on רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. רבי יהושע בן לוי's notebook then opens a new topic: a person's nature depends on the day of the week he was born, based on what was created on that day. רבי חנינא disagrees and says the planet ruling the hour of birth is what matters, and lists the seven planets. Finally, רבי חנינא says the Jewish people are subject to מזל. רבי יוחנן and רב disagree, proving from פסוקים in ירמיהו and from the story of אברהם that אין מזל לישראל. The discussion of אברהם continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The lenient view belongs to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the תנא behind the lenient position on kneading.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the opinion of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers who holds the lenient view that kneading is allowed on שבת. It is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous discussion had a ruling permitting kneading that seemed to clash with the view that one may not knead. By naming the author, the גמרא shows the lenient ruling follows a specific תנא who permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is', used to identify the author of a view

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an identification question from the preceding part of the sugya (previous daf).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the תנא of the lenient view on kneading?

steps.title: The leniency only applies when done differently
steps.stepSummary: The permission to knead is limited to when one changes the normal method.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this only applies where one does it in a changed way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a condition: kneading is only allowed if you do it differently from a weekday. This sets up the next question, 'how?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not permit normal kneading. A שינוי (change in method) is required so the act does not look like ordinary weekday work.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only... (a limiting phrase)
Where one changes the manner of doing it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying kneading is generally allowed. It is only allowed with a שינוי.

phrases.english: And this applies only where one alters (the method).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the lenient view just identified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kneading is permitted only with a change from the usual method.

steps.title: How does one change the kneading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the required change looks like.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one alter it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: what exactly counts as a change?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'do it differently' is not enough. The גמרא wants a concrete, usable method.

phrases.english: How does one alter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the condition just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical form of the שינוי in kneading.

steps.title: רב חסדא: knead a little at a time
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the change is kneading in small amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: little by little.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that you knead a small amount at a time instead of all at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a weekday one kneads the whole batch together. Kneading in small portions is a recognizable change, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Little by little, a bit at a time

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A little at a time, a little at a time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: עַל יָד עַל יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how to change.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Knead in small portions rather than all at once.

steps.title: All agree one may stir שתית and drink Egyptian beer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states agreement that stirring שתית and drinking זיתום המצרי are permitted on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that one may stir שתית on שבת and drink Egyptian beer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that everyone agrees stirring שתית (a roasted-grain mixture) on שבת is allowed, and so is drinking Egyptian beer. This sets up a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They agree' means even those who are strict elsewhere permit these things. Egyptian beer is drunk as a normal drink, so it is not treated as forbidden medicine.

keyTerms.meaning: A dish of roasted grain flour mixed with liquid
Egyptian beer, a drink made from barley and other ingredients

phrases.english: And they agree that one may stir the shatit on Shabbat
and drink Egyptian beer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new source on mixing שתית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stirring שתית and drinking זיתום המצרי on שבת are agreed to be permitted.

steps.title: But we said one may not knead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from the rule that one may not knead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say 'one may not knead'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that stirring שתית seems to contradict the rule forbidding kneading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stirring flour and liquid together looks a lot like kneading. If kneading is forbidden, how can everyone permit stirring שתית?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: But didn't you say 'one may not knead'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The agreement that stirring שתית is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stirring שתית resembles kneading, which was stated to be forbidden.

steps.title: Thick versus thin mixture
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition is for a thick mixture; the permission is for a thin one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this is with a thick mixture, that is with a thin one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: kneading is forbidden for a thick mixture, while stirring is allowed for a thin, runny one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thick mixture is actually like dough, so it counts as kneading. A thin mixture is just a liquid being stirred, so the agreement to permit applies to it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces a resolution)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is with a thick (mixture), that is with a thin one.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּעָבָה, הָא בְּרַכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Stirring שתית and kneading are the same act, so the sources conflict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thick mixture is kneading; thin mixture is mere stirring and is permitted.

steps.title: Again, only with a change
steps.stepSummary: The permission to stir is also limited to doing it differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only where one alters the method.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same condition: even this stirring is allowed only in a changed way. This sets up another 'how?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא really does repeat the phrase here, now applying it to stirring שתית. Even a thin mixture still needs a שינוי.

phrases.english: And this applies only where one alters (the method).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the permission in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stirring permitted mixtures also requires a שינוי.

steps.title: How does one change the stirring?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the method of change for שתית.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one alter it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again asks what the change looks like, now for שתית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method for dough (little by little) may not fit a liquid dish, so a new answer is needed.

phrases.english: How does one alter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details of step 8's condition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical שינוי for preparing שתית.

steps.title: רב יוסף: reverse the order of ingredients
steps.stepSummary: On weekdays vinegar goes first; on שבת the שתית goes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: on a weekday one puts in the vinegar and then the שתית; on שבת one puts in the שתית and then the vinegar.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that the change is reversing the order: on שבת you put the grain in first and then the vinegar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply swapping the order of ingredients is enough to make the act clearly different from weekday preparation.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
On a weekday one places the vinegar
and afterward places the shatit;
on Shabbat one places the shatit
and afterward places the vinegar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בַּחוֹל נוֹתֵן אֶת הַחוֹמֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reverse the weekday order: שתית first, then vinegar.
steps.whatToRemember: A שינוי can be very simple, like reversing the order of ingredients.

steps.title: לוי stops a worker feeding the ox
steps.stepSummary: לוי found his family's kneader kneading and feeding the ox on שבת, and kicked him.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי, son of רב הונא בר חייא, found the kneader of his household kneading and feeding the ox. He kicked him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: לוי saw a worker kneading feed and hand-feeding the ox on שבת, and he kicked him to stop him. This sets up the father's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי assumed the whole activity was forbidden. The story shows a real-life application of the laws of kneading animal feed.

keyTerms.term: לֵוִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא
keyTerms.meaning: לוי, son of רב הונא בר חייא
The kneader, a worker who prepares dough or feed

phrases.aramaic: לֵוִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Levi, son of Rav Huna bar Chiyya,
found the kneader of his household
who was kneading and feeding it to his ox.
He kicked him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵוִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְגַבָּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from human food to animal feed through a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: kneading and hand-feeding an ox on שבת.

steps.title: Knead but do not hand-feed, except a calf
steps.stepSummary: The father cites רבי ירמיה בר אבא in the name of רב: one may knead but not hand-feed, but an animal that cannot eat by itself may be fed.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father came and found him. He said: Your mother's father said in the name of רב (and who is that? רבי ירמיה בר אבא): One may knead but not hand-feed, and an animal that does not take food with its tongue may be fed.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי's father explains the actual law: kneading the feed was fine, but stuffing food into the ox's mouth was not. An animal that cannot take food with its tongue, like a young calf, may be fed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So לוי was partly right: the feeding was wrong, but the kneading was allowed. The גמרא also interrupts to identify 'your mother's father' as רבי ירמיה בר אבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Hand-feed (putting food into an animal's mouth)
Feed directly, for an animal that cannot pick up food itself

phrases.english: His father came and found him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר אֲבוּהּ דְּאִמָּךְ
phrases.english: he said to him: Thus said your mother's father
in the name of Rav,
and who is he? Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba:
phrases.notes: The גמרא breaks in here to tell us who the grandfather is.

phrases.english: One may knead but not hand-feed,
and one that does not take with its tongue, may be fed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר אֲבוּהּ דְּאִמָּךְ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects לוי's reaction in step 11 with the actual halacha.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kneading animal feed is permitted; hand-feeding is not, unless the animal cannot take food with its tongue.
steps.confusionAlert: The father is not saying the worker did everything right. Kneading was allowed; hand-feeding the ox was not.

steps.title: Kneading feed also requires a change
steps.stepSummary: The permission to knead animal feed is limited to doing it differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only where one alters the method.
steps.whatsHappening: Once more the גמרא adds that kneading animal feed is allowed only with a change. This sets up the third 'how?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same condition, repeated a third time, now applies to animal feed.

phrases.english: And this applies only where one alters (the method).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the permission in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kneading animal feed requires a שינוי.

steps.title: How does one change the feed kneading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the method of change for animal feed.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one alter it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical change when kneading animal feed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new kind of mixture needs its own concrete method.

phrases.english: How does one alter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details of step 13's condition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical שינוי for kneading animal feed.

steps.title: Stir crosswise
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר בר שלמיא, quoting אביי, says to stir in a crisscross pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר בר שלמיא said in the name of אביי: warp and woof.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is to stir in straight crossing lines, like the threads of a weave, instead of the usual circular motion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal stirring goes around in circles. Moving the spoon back and forth in straight lines is a noticeable change.

keyTerms.meaning: Warp and woof: lengthwise and crosswise lines, as in weaving

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya said in the name of Abaye:
Warp and woof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי: שְׁתִי וָעֵרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.

steps.title: But that won't mix well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that crosswise stirring does not mix properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it won't mix well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the method: stirring in straight lines will not mix the feed properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שינוי should still let the job get done. If crosswise stirring leaves the mixture unmixed, it is not a practical solution.

phrases.english: But it does not mix well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method of step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Straight-line stirring will not blend the mixture, so the method is impractical.

steps.title: רב יהודה: pour it into another vessel
steps.stepSummary: The mixing is done by pouring from one vessel into another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: one pours it into a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains that the mixing happens by pouring the contents into another vessel, which blends them well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring from one container to another mixes everything thoroughly while still being different from normal stirring. This solves the problem raised in step 16.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
He pours it out into a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שתי וערב stirring alone would leave the mixture poorly mixed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pouring into another vessel mixes it well and still counts as a שינוי.
steps.whatToRemember: Every permitted kneading or mixing on שבת needs a שינוי. There are three methods: little by little (dough), reversing ingredient order (שתית), and crosswise stirring or pouring between vessels (animal feed).

steps.title: זעירי's notebook: kneading is forbidden, emptying is allowed
steps.stepSummary: זעירי records that he asked רבי חייא two questions. Kneading on שבת is forbidden. Emptying feed out of a vessel in front of one animal to give it to another is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was written in זעירי's notebook: I said before my teacher (who is that? רבי חייא): What is the law about kneading? He said: forbidden. What is the law about emptying out? He said: permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a written record from זעירי's notebook. It contains two rulings he heard from his teacher רבי חייא about animal feed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps allowed kneading animal feed only when done differently. Here רבי חייא simply says 'forbidden' to kneading, probably meaning the normal way. He permits 'פירוק': taking food out of one animal's trough and placing it before another animal, which involves no real מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A notebook in which a חכם wrote down rulings he heard
To knead (mix flour or feed with liquid)
To empty out (move feed from one trough to another animal)
'And who is he?' The גמרא identifies an unnamed person

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'וּמַנּוּ — רַבִּי חִיָּיא' are not part of the notebook. They are the גמרא interrupting to tell you who 'my teacher' was.

phrases.english: It was written in Zeiri's notebook:
I said before my teacher,
and who is that? Rabbi Chiya:
phrases.notes: The גמרא breaks in here to tell us who the teacher is.

phrases.english: What is the law about kneading? He said: forbidden.
What is the law about emptying out? He said: permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a recorded tradition about feeding animals on שבת, continuing the topic of kneading animal feed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kneading is forbidden; emptying feed from before one animal to give to another is permitted.

steps.title: רב מנשיא limits how much may be emptied
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא says one trough before one animal, or two before two, is fine. Three troughs before two animals is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא said: one before one, two before two, is fine. Three before two is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא puts a limit on the permission to empty feed that רבי חייא just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting out feed is allowed when it matches the animals' needs. Giving two animals three troughs is more than they need, so it counts as unnecessary effort (טרחה) on שבת and is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Menashya said:

phrases.aramaic: חַד קַמֵּי חַד, תְּרֵי קַמֵּי תְּרֵי —
phrases.english: One before one, two before two —
it is fine.
Three before two — forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא: חַד קַמֵּי חַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the limits of the permission 'לפרק' from step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feed may be set out only in proportion to the animals present; three troughs for two animals is forbidden.

steps.title: רב יוסף and עולא allow larger amounts
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף allows a קב or even two קבים. עולא allows a כור or even two כורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: a קב, and even two קבים. עולא said: a כור, and even two כורים.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more אמוראים give their own, more lenient views about how much feed may be handled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב מנשיא, who limits by the number of animals, רב יוסף allows even an extra קב or two. עולא goes much further and allows a כור or two, a very large amount. Each opinion is more lenient than the one before it.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A kav, and even two kav.
Ulla said:
A kor, and even two kor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: קַב וַאֲפִילּוּ קַבַּיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers more lenient positions than רב מנשיא on the same question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף permits up to two קבים; עולא permits even two כורים.

steps.title: לוי's notebook: רבי protested kneading שתיתא but could not stop it
steps.stepSummary: לוי records that רבי cried out against people in בבל kneading שתיתא on שבת. No one listened, and he could not forbid it because people relied on רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was written in לוי's notebook: I said before my teacher (who is that? רבינו הקדוש) about people kneading שתיתא in בבל. רבי cried out (who? רבינו הקדוש, about their kneading שתיתא), but no one listened to him. He did not have the power to forbid it, because of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second notebook, this one from לוי. It tells how רבי objected to a Babylonian kneading practice on שבת and failed to stop it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי held that kneading שתיתא (a dish of roasted flour mixed with liquid) is forbidden. However, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה had permitted it, and people relied on his opinion. Even the great רבי could not overturn a practice backed by a legitimate תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our holy teacher,' a title for רבי יהודה הנשיא
A dish of roasted flour mixed with water or honey

steps.confusionAlert: The part in parentheses repeats the identification of רבי. It is the גמרא clarifying who protested, not a second event.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that once a practice rests on a recognized תנא's view, even a great leader cannot simply forbid it.

phrases.english: It was written in Levi's notebook:
I said before my teacher,
and who is that? Our holy teacher,
about the fact that they would knead shatit in Babylonia,
and my teacher would cry out
(and who is that? Our holy teacher,
about their kneading shatit),
and there was no one who listened to him,
and he did not have the power to forbid it
because of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second notebook record on kneading on שבת, parallel to זעירי's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי forbade kneading שתיתא, but the practice continued based on רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's permission.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי's notebook: one born on Sunday
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי's notebook says that a person born on Sunday will be a man 'with no one in him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was written in רבי יהושע בן לוי's notebook: Someone born on the first day of the week will be a man, and there will not be one in him.
steps.whatsHappening: Moving from one notebook to another, the גמרא shifts to a new topic: how the day of birth affects a person's nature. This unclear statement sets up the next steps, which try to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new subject is linked to the earlier material only because it also comes from a פנקס. The key phrase 'ולא חדא ביה' is unclear, and the גמרא will spend the next steps working out its meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: On the first day of the week (Sunday)
And there will not be 'one' in him (unclear phrase)

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב אַפִּינְקָסֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: It was written in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's notebook:
One who is born on the first day of the week,
will be a man, and there will not be one in him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב אַפִּינְקָסֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a new, אגדה topic, linked only by the shared notebook format
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person born on Sunday will be 'a man with no one in him.'

steps.title: What does 'there will not be one in him' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'ולא חדא ביה' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and there will not be one in him' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear phrase. This sets up a series of suggested answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'one' could refer to a single good trait or a single bad trait. The גמרא will test each possibility against real-life cases.

phrases.english: What is 'and there will not be one in him'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the statement in step 22

steps.title: It cannot mean 'not one good trait,' because of רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: First suggestion: he will not have even one good trait. This is rejected, because רב אשי was born on Sunday.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means 'not one for good,' but רב אשי said: I was born on the first day of the week!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first reading, that such a person has nothing good in him. It immediately rejects this reading with a counter-example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי, a great Torah leader, said he was born on Sunday. It is impossible to say he had no good qualities, so this reading fails.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be tested)
But didn't (so-and-so) say? Introduces a counter-source

phrases.english: If you say: not one for good,
but Rav Ashi said:
I was born on the first day of the week!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects the first answer to step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading 'no good trait at all'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אשי was born on Sunday and was clearly good

steps.title: It cannot mean 'not one bad trait,' because of דימי בר קקוזתא
steps.stepSummary: Second suggestion: he will not have even one bad trait. This is rejected, because רב אשי said that he and דימי בר קקוזתא were both born on Sunday. רב אשי became a king and דימי became a chief of thieves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means 'not one for bad.' But רב אשי said: I and דימי בר קקוזתא were born on the first day of the week. I became a king, and he became the head of thieves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the opposite reading, that such a person has nothing bad in him. It rejects this too, using another statement of רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דימי בר קקוזתא was also born on Sunday, and he became a leader of thieves, which is clearly bad. So Sunday-born people can be bad, and this reading fails as well. 'King' here refers to רב אשי's leadership as head of the ישיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A man born on Sunday who became a gang leader

phrases.english: Rather, not one for bad,
but Rav Ashi said:
I and Dimi bar Kakuzta
were born on the first day of the week,

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא מֶלֶךְ, וְהוּא הֲוָה רֵישׁ גַּנָּבֵי!
phrases.english: I became a king, and he became the head of thieves!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first reading failed, proposes and rejects the opposite reading
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading 'no bad trait at all'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: דימי בר קקוזתא was born on Sunday and became a chief of thieves

steps.title: Conclusion: either completely good or completely bad
steps.stepSummary: The phrase means that a Sunday-born person is all one way: entirely good or entirely bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: either all of him is for good, or all of him is for bad.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected both earlier readings, the גמרא gives the correct meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not one in him' means there is no mixture inside him. Such a person goes to an extreme in one direction. This fits both רב אשי (fully good) and דימי (fully bad).
steps.whatToRemember: A person born on Sunday is not a mix of traits. He is either entirely good or entirely bad.

phrases.english: Rather: either all of him is for good,
or all of him is for bad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question after both alternatives were rejected
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One born on Sunday will be either completely good or completely bad.

steps.title: The reason: light and darkness were created on Sunday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that this is because both light and darkness were created on the first day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because light and darkness were created on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a Sunday-born person goes to extremes and answers in the same breath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day of Creation, both light and darkness were made, two complete opposites. A person born on that day takes on that nature: he will be fully 'light' (good) or fully 'darkness' (bad), not a blend.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the pattern for the rest of this passage: each weekday's character comes from what was created on that day.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because light and darkness were created on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּאִיבְּרוֹ בֵּיהּ אוֹר וָחוֹשֶׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the conclusion in step 26
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a Sunday-born person is all good or all bad
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the opposites of light and darkness were both created on Sunday

steps.title: Born on Monday: short-tempered
steps.stepSummary: A person born on Monday will be short-tempered, because the waters were divided on the second day of Creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born on Monday will be a short-tempered man. Why? Because on that day the waters were split apart.
steps.whatsHappening: The list moves from Sunday to Monday. It gives a trait and then the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as Sunday: the trait comes from what happened on that day of Creation. On the second day the upper and lower waters were separated. That division points to a nature full of conflict and anger.

keyTerms.meaning: The second day of the week, Monday

phrases.english: One who is born on the second day of the week
will be a short-tempered man.
What is the reason?
Because on it the waters were divided.
phrases.notes: The upper and lower waters were separated on the second day of Creation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the day-by-day list after Sunday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Monday-born people are short-tempered, because division happened on that day.

steps.title: Born on Tuesday: rich and promiscuous
steps.stepSummary: A person born on Tuesday will be wealthy and promiscuous, because vegetation was created on the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born on Tuesday will be rich and promiscuous. Why? Because plants were created on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with Tuesday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plants grow in huge amounts, which points to wealth. They also grow mixed together with no boundaries between them, which points to a lack of restraint.

phrases.english: One who is born on the third day of the week
will be a rich man, and he will be promiscuous.
What is the reason?
Because vegetation was created on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next day in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tuesday-born people are wealthy and promiscuous, like plants that grow abundantly and intermixed.

steps.title: Born on Wednesday: wise and bright
steps.stepSummary: A person born on Wednesday will be wise and enlightened, because the lights were hung in the sky on the fourth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born on Wednesday will be wise and bright. Why? Because the sun, moon, and stars were hung up on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with Wednesday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wisdom is often compared to light. Since the heavenly lights were placed on this day, a person born then will be 'bright', meaning wise.

phrases.english: One who is born on the fourth day of the week
will be a wise and enlightened man.
What is the reason?
Because the lights were hung on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next day in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wednesday-born people are wise, connected to the creation of the lights.

steps.title: Born on Thursday: does kindness
steps.stepSummary: A person born on Thursday will do acts of kindness, because fish and birds were created on the fifth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born on Thursday will be a man who does kindness. Why? Because fish and birds were created on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with Thursday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish and birds do not work for people to earn their food. They are fed by ה׳'s kindness alone. So a person born on that day will be marked by kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: One who does acts of kindness

phrases.english: One who is born on the fifth day of the week
will be a man who does acts of kindness.
What is the reason?
Because fish and birds were created on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next day in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thursday-born people do kindness, like creatures sustained by ה׳'s kindness.

steps.title: Born on Friday: a seeker of מצוות
steps.stepSummary: A person born on Friday will be a 'seeker'. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that this means a seeker of מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born on Friday will be a seeker. רב נחמן בר יצחק said: a seeker of מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with Friday. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the unclear word חזרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No reason from Creation is given here. The word 'seeker' could sound negative, so רב נחמן בר יצחק makes clear that it means someone who chases after מצוות. Friday is a day of running around preparing for שבת.

phrases.english: One who is born on Friday
will be a seeker.
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
A seeker of מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next day in the list, plus a clarification of the key word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Friday-born people pursue מצוות.

steps.title: Born on שבת: dies on שבת, called holy
steps.stepSummary: A person born on שבת will die on שבת, because שבת was desecrated for his birth. רבא בר רב שילא adds that he will be called a great holy person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born on שבת will die on שבת, because the great day of שבת was desecrated for him. רבא בר רב שילא said: and he will be called a great holy one.
steps.whatsHappening: The list ends with שבת. רבא בר רב שילא adds a positive side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a baby is born on שבת, people do מלאכה to help the mother. The first statement links his death to that חילול שבת. רבא בר רב שילא balances it: being born on the holy day also makes him holy.
steps.whatToRemember: The day-of-the-week list: each day's trait comes from what was created on that day, ending with שבת.

phrases.english: One who is born on Shabbos
will die on Shabbos,
because they desecrated on his account
the great day of Shabbos.
Rava bar Rav Sheila said:
And he will be called a great holy one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final day of the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שבת-born person dies on שבת and is called holy.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: the hour matters, not the day
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא sends a message to רבי יהושע בן לוי: a person's nature is set by the planet of the hour he was born in, and not by the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said to them: Go tell בר ליואי: the מזל of the day does not decide. The מזל of the hour decides.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא rejects the whole day-of-the-week system. This sets up a new list based on the hour of birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each hour is ruled by one of seven planets in a fixed cycle. רבי חנינא holds that this hour-planet is what shapes a person, and not the day. The next steps go through each planet one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: Nickname for רבי יהושע בן לוי
The planetary sign of the hour

steps.confusionAlert: בר ליואי is not a new person. It is רבי יהושע בן לוי, whose notebook was the source of the day-of-the-week list.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said to them,
Go and tell the son of Leivai:
It is not the constellation of the day that determines,
rather the constellation of the hour determines.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא מַזַּל יוֹם גּוֹרֵם אֶלָּא מַזַּל שָׁעָה גּוֹרֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the day-based system just listed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The day is the wrong factor. The hour's planet is what determines a person's nature.

steps.title: Born under the sun: radiant and open
steps.stepSummary: A person born in the sun's hour is radiant, lives from his own resources, and has no secrets. If he steals, he will not succeed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born under חמה will be a radiant man. He will eat and drink from his own, his secrets will be out in the open, and if he steals he won't succeed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא begins his hour-based list with the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sun shines with its own light and is seen by everyone. So this person is independent and open. He cannot hide anything, which is why stealing won't work for him.

phrases.english: One who is born under the sun
will be a radiant man,
he will eat from his own and drink from his own,
and his secrets will be exposed;
if he steals, he will not succeed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First item in רבי חנינא's hour list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sun-born people are independent and transparent.

steps.title: Born under Venus: rich and promiscuous
steps.stepSummary: A person born in the hour of כוכב נוגה (Venus) is wealthy and promiscuous, because fire was created in that hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born under כוכב נוגה will be rich and promiscuous. Why? Because fire was born in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The hour list continues with Venus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire was brought into being in Venus's hour. Fire hints at a burning, unrestrained desire, the יצר הרע. This matches the same traits given earlier for Tuesday.

phrases.english: One who is born under Venus
will be a rich man, and he will be promiscuous.
What is the reason?
Because fire was born in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next planet in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Venus-born people are wealthy and driven by desire.

steps.title: Born under Mercury: bright and wise
steps.stepSummary: A person born in the hour of כוכב (Mercury) is bright and wise, because Mercury is the sun's scribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born under כוכב will be bright and wise, because it is the sun's scribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The hour list continues with Mercury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mercury is the planet closest to the sun, like a secretary at the king's side. A scribe is a wise, learned person, so a person born in this hour is wise.

phrases.english: One who is born under Mercury
will be an enlightened and wise man,
because it is the sun's scribe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next planet in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mercury-born people are wise.

steps.title: Born under the moon: unstable and hidden
steps.stepSummary: A person born in the moon's hour suffers, builds and destroys, lives off others, and keeps secrets. If he steals, he succeeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born under לבנה will suffer pains. He builds and tears down, tears down and builds. He eats and drinks what isn't his, his secrets are hidden, and if he steals he succeeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The hour list continues with the moon, the opposite of the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The moon keeps changing shape, so this person's life goes up and down. The moon's light is borrowed from the sun, so he lives off others. The moon is sometimes hidden, so his secrets stay hidden and stealing works for him.

phrases.english: One who is born under the moon
will be a man who suffers pains,
he builds and destroys, destroys and builds,
he eats what is not his
and drinks what is not his,
and his secrets are hidden;
if he steals, he succeeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next planet, written as a mirror image of the sun.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moon-born people are unstable, dependent, and secretive.

steps.title: Born under Saturn: plans come to nothing
steps.stepSummary: A person born in the hour of שבתאי (Saturn) has his plans fail. Others say that the plans others make against him fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born under שבתאי will be a man whose thoughts come to nothing. Some say: whatever others plan against him comes to nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The hour list continues with Saturn, and two opinions are given about what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name שבתאי is related to 'stopping' (שבת). The first opinion reads this negatively: his own plans stop. The יש אומרים reads it positively: plots against him stop.

phrases.english: One who is born under Saturn
will be a man whose thoughts come to nothing.
And some say:
Everything that others plan against him comes to nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next planet in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saturn's hour causes plans to be canceled, either his own or those made against him.

steps.title: Born under Jupiter: righteous in מצוות
steps.stepSummary: A person born in the hour of צדק (Jupiter) will be a צדקן. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that this means righteous in מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born under צדק will be a righteous man. רב נחמן בר יצחק said: righteous in מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The hour list continues with Jupiter. רב נחמן בר יצחק again explains the key word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The planet's name, צדק, is matched to the trait צדקן. רב נחמן בר יצחק specifies that it means doing מצוות, just as he explained חזרן earlier for Friday.

phrases.english: One who is born under Jupiter
will be a righteous man.
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
And righteous in מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next planet in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jupiter-born people are righteous in מצוות.

steps.title: Born under Mars: sheds blood
steps.stepSummary: A person born in the hour of מאדים (Mars) will shed blood. רב אשי lists four ways: bloodletter, thief, butcher, or מוהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever is born under מאדים will be a man who spills blood. רב אשי said: either a bloodletter, a thief, a butcher, or a מוהל.
steps.whatsHappening: The last planet is Mars. רב אשי shows that 'shedding blood' does not have to mean murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mars is red, the color of blood. רב אשי shows that this drive can go into a bad outlet (theft) or into good or neutral ones (medicine, שחיטה, מילה).

phrases.english: One who is born under Mars
will be a man who spills blood.
Rav Ashi said:
either a bloodletter, or a thief,
or a slaughterer, or a circumciser.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final planet in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mars-born people are drawn to bloodshed, which can be directed into permitted professions.

steps.title: רבה: I was born under Mars
steps.stepSummary: רבה says he was born under מאדים, hinting that he does none of the four blood-related jobs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: I was born under מאדים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה uses himself as a challenge to the Mars rule. He is not a bloodletter, thief, butcher, or מוהל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His statement is short, but its function is a challenge. If the rule is true, how does רבה fit? This sets up אביי's answer.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
I was born under Mars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the Mars rule against a real person.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that Mars-born people shed blood, with רב אשי's list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה was born under Mars but does none of the listed blood-related activities.

steps.title: אביי: you punish and execute as a judge
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבה also sheds blood, because as a judge he punishes and sentences people to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Master, you too punish and kill.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves רבה's challenge by showing that רבה does fit the Mars pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As a דיין, רבה punishes people who break the law, and the text calls this 'killing'. That counts as 'shedding blood' in a permitted, holy way, so the rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The planet gives a tendency. How it shows up can be good or bad, as with רבה the judge.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The Master also punishes and kills.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening the category to include judicial punishment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה seems to break the Mars rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה's work as a judge is his form of 'shedding blood'.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: מזל affects Jews too
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says that מזל makes a person wise and wealthy, and that the Jewish people are subject to מזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי חנינא says: מזל makes wise, מזל makes rich, and there is מזל for ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens: does מזל control the Jewish people? רבי חנינא says yes. This sets up a dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches רבי חנינא's hour-based view from before. He extends it to say that wisdom and wealth come from מזל, and that Jews are not exempt from it.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Chanina says:
A constellation makes one wise, a constellation makes one wealthy,
and there is a constellation for Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new dispute built on רבי חנינא's view of מזל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jews are subject to מזל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: no מזל for Jews
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and says the Jewish people are not under מזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: There is no מזל for ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposing side of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He holds that the stars have no control over Jews. Their fate depends directly on ה׳, through their deeds and תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Israel is not under the stars' control

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
There is no constellation for Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view to רבי חנינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jews are not subject to מזל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source from ירמיהו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן is consistent with another statement of his, where he proves from a פסוק in ירמיהו that only the nations fear the heavenly signs, and not ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, because he said: How do we know Jews have no מזל? The פסוק says: 'Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be frightened by signs of the sky, because the nations are frightened by them.' They will be frightened, not ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs רבי יוחנן's view with his own proof from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells ישראל not to fear the heavenly signs, and says that the nations fear them. רבי יוחנן reads this as: the stars rule over the nations, but not over ישראל.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the discussion. The very next step shows that רב also agrees with רבי יוחנן, using a פסוק about אברהם.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא: Jews are under מזל. רבי יוחנן: they are not, based on ירמיהו 10:2.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:
From where do we know that there is no constellation for Israel?
As it says: "Thus said ה׳:
Do not learn the way of the nations,
and do not be dismayed by the signs of the heavens,
for the nations are dismayed by them"
They will be dismayed, but not Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for רבי יוחנן's position.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that Jews are not under מזל
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 10:2, which says the nations fear the heavenly signs and ישראל should not

steps.title: רב also holds there is no מזל for Israel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a statement of רב, through רב יהודה, showing that רב agrees with רבי יוחנן. רב learns it from the פסוק 'ויוצא אותו החוצה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב also holds that there is no מזל for ישראל. As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: From where do we know that there is no מזל for ישראל? Because it says, 'And He brought him outside.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second אמורא, רב, to the side of רבי יוחנן, who says the Jewish people are not ruled by the stars. It quotes the פסוק רב uses as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 46, רבי יוחנן was shown to be consistent with his own other statement. Now the גמרא shows that רב holds the same view, so רבי חנינא's opinion stands against two אמוראים. Right now we only have the פסוק; the explanation of how it proves the point comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: And also, meaning this person agrees too
The Jewish people are not controlled by the stars or planets
From where do we know? (a request for a source)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'outside' here as only meaning outside the tent. רב reads it as 'outside your astrology.' That is explained in step 49.

phrases.english: And Rav also holds
there is no constellation (mazal) for Israel,
as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
From where do we know that there is no mazal for Israel?
As it is stated: 'And He brought him outside,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 15:5. In that verse God shows אברהם the stars.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב סָבַר אֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רב as another supporter of רבי יוחנן's view from step 45, right after step 46 showed רבי יוחנן is consistent with himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב holds that ישראל is not under מזל, learned from 'ויוצא אותו החוצה.'

steps.title: אברהם worries his servant will inherit him
steps.stepSummary: רב explains the background: אברהם complained that his household servant would be his heir. הקדוש ברוך הוא answered that his heir would come from his own body.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world, 'one born in my house will inherit me.' He said to him: No, 'rather, one who comes out of your own body' will inherit you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב starts telling the story behind the פסוק. This step sets the scene for the main point in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם thinks he will die childless, so his servant will inherit him (בראשית ט״ו:ג). הקדוש ברוך הוא promises him a biological son (ט״ו:ד). This creates the problem the next step deals with: how can אברהם have a son if the stars say he cannot?

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the world (a way of addressing God)
One born in my house, meaning a household servant (אליעזר)
From your innards, meaning your own biological child

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבְרָהָם לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Avraham said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
'one born in my house is to be my heir,'
He said to him: No —
'rather, one that will come forth from your own innards.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבְרָהָם לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the background of the פסוק רב quoted in step 47.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא promised אברהם a son from his own body, not the servant as heir.

steps.title: Step outside your astrology, because Israel has no מזל
steps.stepSummary: אברהם says his astrology shows he cannot have a son. הקדוש ברוך הוא tells him to leave his astrology, because ישראל is not under מזל. That is the meaning of 'He brought him outside.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said before Him: Master of the world, I looked at my astrology, and I am not fit to have a son. He said to him: Go out of your astrology, because there is no מזל for ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of רב's proof. 'He brought him outside' means God took אברהם outside the control of the stars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם's objection is that his star chart says no son is possible. God's answer does not say the chart was wrong. It says the chart does not apply to ישראל. This is what makes the פסוק a proof that אין מזל לישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out of your astrology (the reading of 'החוצה')

steps.whatToRemember: רב reads 'ויוצא אותו החוצה' as God taking אברהם outside of astrology. This is רב's source that the Jewish people are not ruled by מזל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This puts רב firmly with רבי יוחנן against רבי חנינא, and it bases the idea on the founding promise to אברהם.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
I looked at my astrological map,
and I am not fit to have a son.
He said to him: Emerge from your astrology,
as there is no mazal for Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: צֵא מֵאִיצְטַגְנִינוּת שֶׁלְּךָ שֶׁאֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 48 and shows how the פסוק from step 47 proves רב's view.
steps.raayaObject: רב's position that אין מזל לישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reading of 'ויוצא אותו החוצה' (בראשית ט״ו:ה) as 'go out of your astrology'

steps.title: God asks אברהם what he is thinking
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא begins to ask אברהם what exactly in his star chart made him think he could not have a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are you thinking?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next move. הקדוש ברוך הוא is about to spell out אברהם's astrological worry and answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks אברהם to name the exact star-based reason for his worry. The answer, on the next amud, will show how God overrides that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your thinking? What is your reasoning?

phrases.english: What is your thinking?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues God's reply in step 49 by asking about the specific basis of אברהם's astrological worry.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific astrological reason אברהם believes he cannot have a son
